summary:
ORACLE-Fire is a research workbench that helps people inspect NASA microgravity-combustion studies with experimental context attached to each finding. It searches and retains source records, links candidate observations to supporting passages, and makes study conditions visible when users compare evidence. In its demonstration, the tool explains why GEL PMMA-sphere extinction and BASS fabric-quenching results cannot be treated as one interchangeable oxygen threshold. It also calculates a narrower descriptive contrast between two GEL Table 1 entries: 14.99% and 14.21% oxygen, or 0.78 percentage points, while preserving the conditions that limit interpretation. The workspace supports source inspection, comparison, research briefs, export, and replay of retained evidence. It addresses the challenge of making decades of microgravity-fire research easier to find and interpret for exploration-related research. ORACLE-Fire is a research prototype, not a NASA product or certified spacecraft-safety system.

details:
What it does. ORACLE-Fire is a local research workbench for locating and inspecting evidence about NASA microgravity combustion. It connects a research question to NASA source records, retained source passages, structured experimental observations and an inspectable report. Users can inspect the source and experimental context, compare retained records, open source evidence, view source-linked research briefs, export an investigation and replay it from retained evidence. The browser workspace also preserves the wider ORACLE and LENS experience.

How it addresses Flame in Freefall. The challenge asks for an interactive SI-powered dashboard to summarize, rank and interpret microgravity-combustion findings relevant to human space exploration. ORACLE-Fire makes experimental context part of that interaction. Its comparison explorer distinguishes a descriptive numerical contrast from a controlled comparison, shows missing or different conditions, and retains the evidence behind the result. In the demonstration, it blocks treating GEL PMMA-sphere extinction and BASS fabric-quenching as one interchangeable oxygen threshold, while showing the limited 0.78-percentage-point difference between two values in GEL Table 1. The latter is descriptive; it is not a causal or statistical conclusion.

Why it matters and intended impact. A source quotation or number can be accurate yet apply to a different material, procedure or observable. ORACLE-Fire is designed to help researchers and learners inspect those distinctions while reviewing literature and framing follow-up questions relevant to spacecraft-fire research. Adoption by NASA or other users has not been demonstrated, and this prototype must not be used to set flight-safety limits or guide emergency decisions.

Tools and implementation. The workbench uses Python 3.11, FastAPI/Starlette, SQLite, HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Its research pipeline integrates NASA NTRS and PSI access, optional Exa/Tavily/Serper search, and role-configured Gemini/Groq model calls. The project also preserves pre-existing ORACLE and LENS software and uses local E.V.I.E-derived retrieval/persistence components. Tests use pytest and Playwright. See the resource register for NASA references, software dependencies and external services.

Creative and scientific design choices. The key design decision is to attach evidence scope and experiment conditions to findings, and to ask what kind of comparison is appropriate before calculating. Missing values stay missing; observed outcomes, author interpretations and derived arithmetic remain distinct. Ranking indicates topical relevance/applicability cues, not truth, measurement quality or independent confirmation. A paper/archive agreement for one BASS event is treated as provenance consistency, not independent replication.

Verification. The final local regression recorded 907 passing Python tests with no failures, errors or skips. Browser workflows passed 84 assertions (25 focused checks plus six workflow suites), and a source-specific GEL/BASS reference passed 21/21 checks. These establish engineering and workflow behavior and a small, implementation-curated reference check only. In a separate frozen 12-question paired diagnostic, the hardened release produced useful outputs in 9/12 tasks versus 8/12 for the preserved release. Neither release fully completed any task (0/12), the hardened release had more material unsupported-claim or type errors (3 vs 1), and it acquired the necessary primary source less often (9/12 vs 11/12). That is a small AI-assisted diagnostic, not evidence of superiority. Known limitations: four offline prompt trials returned the same generic conclusion for different prompts, and one fresh Saffire VI prompt selected a noisy secondary page and included irrelevant extracted evidence. No qualified combustion specialist has reviewed the results yet. ORACLE-Fire is a prototype with partially validated scientific behavior, not a generally reliable autonomous scientific answer system.

AI/SI assistance. OpenAI Codex assisted software work, test planning, documentation, science-audit support and submission writing. Gemini/Groq models are used within the research pipeline for bounded extraction/advisory roles. NASA facts and values come from cited NASA resources. The submitted deck uses transcribed source excerpts and original diagrams.
